description: Golden set for the AI System Design Copilot. Queries cover the 6 documented topics (Netflix, Uber, WhatsApp, URL shortener, Twitter, Dropbox), plus capacity-tool prompts and intentional out-of-domain probes.

queries.query: Design a URL shortener like bit.ly. Cover the encoding scheme, database, caching, and how you'd handle billions of links.
Design Twitter's home timeline. Explain the fanout-on-write vs fanout-on-read tradeoff and how you'd handle celebrity users.
Design WhatsApp messaging including 1-1 chats, group chats, presence, and end-to-end encryption.
Design Netflix's video streaming pipeline from upload to playback. Cover transcoding, CDN, and adaptive bitrate.
Design Uber's ride-matching service. Explain how drivers and riders are matched in real time and how location updates are handled.
Design Dropbox's file storage and sync. Cover chunking, deduplication, conflict resolution, and how clients stay in sync.

Design Twitter for 100 million daily active users who write 5 tweets/day and read 100 tweets/day, with an average tweet size of 1 KB. Show concrete QPS and storage estimates and justify your sharding strategy.
Design WhatsApp for 2 billion daily active users sending 40 messages/day averaging 0.5 KB each. Justify your database and message storage choices with explicit numbers.
Design Netflix for 500 million daily active users, each watching on average 2 hours/day at 5000 kbps. Compute the CDN bandwidth and origin storage requirements and design accordingly.
Design Uber for 50 million daily active users with 30 location updates per active trip per hour and an average payload of 0.3 KB. Show QPS and choose appropriate stream-processing infrastructure.
Design a URL shortener for 1 billion writes/month and 50 billion reads/month with an average payload of 0.2 KB. Compute cache hit-ratio impact and choose a database.
Design Dropbox to ingest 1 PB of new files per month from 100 million daily active users uploading on average 0.5 files/day at 10 MB each. Plan storage and bandwidth.
For a Twitter-like service, walk through the fanout-on-write vs fanout-on-read tradeoff. When would you use each, and how would a hybrid approach work?
For Uber's matching service, compare geohashing vs quad-trees vs S2 cells for indexing driver locations. Which would you pick and why?
Explain Netflix's Open Connect CDN strategy. Why peer with ISPs directly, what gets cached at the edge, and how is content prepositioned?
For Dropbox sync, how would you detect file changes efficiently on the client and resolve conflicts when two clients edit the same file offline?
For WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption, explain how the Signal protocol's double ratchet works and what happens when a user adds a new device to an existing group chat.
Take a typical URL shortener design and refine it to add real-time analytics (click counts, geo, referrer). What components do you add and what database choices change?
Refine a Twitter timeline architecture to add full-text search across all tweets in the last 7 days. What infrastructure do you add?
Take a baseline Uber design and add surge pricing. Describe the signals it needs, where the surge-pricing service lives, and how it talks to matching.
Design a quantum-encrypted blockchain for a planetary central bank that settles 10^18 transactions per second.
Design the radiomics pipeline for federated tumor-volume estimation across 200 hospitals with HIPAA-compliant differential privacy.
Design the persistent-world server architecture for an MMORPG with 1 million concurrent players sharing one shard with sub-100ms tick rate.
